headline: Warthogs strike the richest vein, Super Troopers win by 1.14
lede: Week 9 came in loud, pardner. Warthogs hauled up 147.34, the biggest nugget on the whole territory, while Scott's Hype panned out 72.34 and went home with wet boots. And down at the far end of the street, Super Troopers and Justin's Bad Team settled the whole thing by 1.14, which is about the width of a bootlace.
paragraphs: HAWKSRULE rode down on Long Howie and left nothing standing, 143.7 to 81.55, the widest margin of the week at 62.15. The Bills defense put up 27.0 for HAWKSRULE, which makes a third straight win and a 5-4 record look awful comfortable. Long Howie is still 7-2 and still respectable, but Ladd McConkey posted a clean 0.0 and Joe Milton sat on the bench with 12.38; a better arrangement was worth 8.18 and would not have mattered a lick anyhow.

WeBleedOrangeAndBlue made it 7 wins in a row at 139.57 over densmen's 97.88, with Joe Burrow throwing down 33.97 and not a single point wasted, a better lineup was worth 0.0. Burrow also leads all 144 qualifying men in Points Over Expected at +5.7 per game, which is efficiency, luck, or both, and the fella riding him does not much care which. densmen actually got the day's hottest hand in C.J. Stroud at 37.68 and still lost, because the Giants defense sat benched with 26.0 and a better lineup was worth 29.05, the sorriest arrangement in the whole territory. That is 7 straight losses and a 1-8 ledger.

Warthogs topped the week with 147.34, and Jordan Love did the heavy haulin' at 41.29 while e-mans revenge managed 110.91. Warthogs barely left anything behind, 2.0 was all a better lineup was worth, though the 49ers defense did sit there with 25.0 in its pocket. e-mans revenge got 24.0 from the Texans defense but 1.25 from Tucker Kraft, and a tidier lineup was worth 10.5 against a 36.43 margin. Warthogs is 7-2 with 2 straight; e-mans revenge slides to 5-4.

sisu did not need fireworks, just 103.43 and a 22.35 afternoon from Christian Watson, and that was plenty against Scott's Hype and its 72.34, the lowest score in town. Scott's Hype got 14.14 from Michael Penix Jr. as its best man, which tells you the whole sad story, and Mike Washington Jr. chipped in 1.05. Kaleb Johnson sat on the bench with 12.2 and a better lineup was worth 14.0, still a ways shy of the 31.09 margin. sisu is 5-4, Scott's Hype is 3-6 and losing 2 straight.

Jrod piled up 143.03 on Dart Star Orchestra's 119.25, which is a fine score to lose with and a 23.78 margin all the same. Bucky Irving led Jrod with 24.85, and Arvell Reese turned in 22.0, the best defensive showing anybody put up this week. Dart Star Orchestra got 20.75 from Christian McCaffrey, left Blake Corum and his 11.1 on the bench, and drops to 2-7 with 2 losses running. Jrod climbs to 4-5 and cashed a check besides, even with Drake Maye's 18.33 sitting idle.

Aeil beat Zihuatanejo 111.08 to 91.62, and the Seahawks defense was the big earner at 21.0. Neither outfit ran a tight ship: Aeil left Caleb Downs and his 10.5 on the pine for a lineup worth 10.05 more, and Zihuatanejo left AJ Barner and his 13.9 there for a lineup worth 13.2 more. CeeDee Lamb's 22.75 was the best thing Zihuatanejo had going, while Rashod Bateman handed over 0.7. That is 3 losses in a row and 3-6 for Zihuatanejo; Aeil sits at 4-5.

Jack Attack took it from Norskes U Betcha 113.03 to 99.39 on the back of Puka Nacua's 24.5, and did it with Patrick Mahomes and his 20.24 watching from the wagon seat. A better lineup was worth 17.46 to Jack Attack, which is more than the 13.64 margin, so that was a closer shave than the winner knows. Norskes U Betcha had the same affliction, Tyler Shough and his 20.45 benched while Chad Ryland kicked in 3.0, and the Jaguars defense led the way with 20.0. Jack Attack is 5-4, Norskes U Betcha falls to 3-6.

Super Troopers and Justin's Bad Team went hand to hand all day and the ledger closed at 115.59 to 114.45, a margin of 1.14, closest in the territory. Brock Purdy's 26.24 carried Super Troopers to a second straight win and a 6-3 record, though Jaylen Waddle's 1.5 nearly cost the whole claim. Justin's Bad Team got a thumping 31.35 from Kenneth Walker III and ran a perfect lineup, 0.0 left on the table, and lost anyway. That, pardner, is the cruelest way there is to go to 5-4.
sign_off: 4 weeks left in the regular season and 8 wagons make the playoff trail. Check your lineups before you check your luck.
purse: The commissioner's strongbox opens for 4 this week: Warthogs first at 147.34 for $40, HAWKSRULE second at 143.7 for $20, Jrod third at 143.03 for $10, and WeBleedOrangeAndBlue fourth at 139.57 for $5. WeBleedOrangeAndBlue has now been in the money 6 weeks, Warthogs and Jrod 4 apiece, and HAWKSRULE finally got its name in the ledger for the first time.
